paragraphs: Before the war, there was a balance between the old countries of Europe and the new lands with many resources. But even then, this balance was in danger. Europe was rich for two reasons. First, America had a lot of extra food to sell. So Europe could buy food at a low price. Europe made goods and sold them to other countries. It did not need much work to pay for its food in this way. Second, Europe had put money into other countries in the past. Because of this, it got a lot of money every year. It did not have to give anything back for this money. The second reason seemed safe at that time. But the first reason was not so safe. The number of people across the ocean was growing, mostly in the United States.

When people first grew food on the new land of America, very few people lived there. So they needed only a little food for themselves, compared to Europe. In 1890, Europe still had three times more people than North and South America together. But by 1914, things were different. The United States needed almost all the wheat that it grew. Soon it would have extra wheat to sell only in years with a very good harvest. Today, people think that the United States needs more than ninety per cent of the wheat it grew each year from 1909 to 1913. But at that time, the problem was not too little wheat. The problem was that wheat cost more and more. In the whole world, there was enough wheat. But to get enough of it, buyers had to pay a higher real price. One thing helped Europe a lot. Central and Western Europe got much of its food from Russia and Roumania. These countries had extra food to sell.

So Europe could not be sure of the food from the New World any more. Each year, the land gave less for the same work. Europe had to give more and more goods to get the same amount of bread. Because of this, Europe could not lose any of its main sources of food.

There are many other things to say about Europe in 1914. I have chosen the three or four biggest dangers. First, there were too many people. They needed a difficult and unnatural system to live. Second, workers and rich owners were not calm in their minds. Third, Europe needed food from the New World completely, but it could not be sure of this food.

The war shook this system very badly. It put the life of Europe in danger. A large part of the Continent was sick and dying. There were many more people than there was work and food for them. The system did not work any more. Trains and ships could not move goods well. The food supply was in very bad shape.
